mainEntity.name: How much does a Peugeot 508 1.6 THP engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Peugeot 508 1.6 THP replacement engine typically costs £550-£1,200 for a used unit, £1,100-£1,900 for a reconditioned unit, or £1,900-£3,500 for a rebuilt unit with 12-month warranty. Supply & fit labour adds approximately £400-£800.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a Peugeot 508 1.6 THP?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common sign is a rattling noise from the engine on cold start, lasting 2-3 seconds. Other symptoms include rough idling, loss of power, and the engine management light illuminating. If left unaddressed, timing chain failure can cause catastrophic engine damage.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Peugeot 508 1.6 THP?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a 508 1.6 THP worth £4,000-£12,000, replacement is often worthwhile if the rest of the car is in good condition. If the vehicle is worth under £4,000, a used engine or scrapping may be more cost-effective. One owner reported a £3,500 repair bill for timing chain failure on a 1.6 THP.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Peugeot 508 1.6 THP engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most Peugeot 508 1.6 THP engines are dispatched within 24-48 hours, with supply & fit installation typically completed within 1-2 working days at approved garages.

mainEntity.name: What warranty comes with Peugeot 508 1.6 THP replacement engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: Rebuilt Peugeot 508 1.6 THP engines include a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Used engines typically carry 3-6 months cover depending on supplier terms. Always verify warranty terms before purchase.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the 1.6 THP and the 1.6 PureTech in the Peugeot 508?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 1.6 THP (EP6DT/EP6CDT) was fitted to the first-generation 508 (2010-2018) and is known for timing chain tensioner issues, turbocharger oil leaks and increased oil consumption. The 1.6 PureTech (EP6FDT) replaced it on the second-generation 508 (2018 onwards), offering improved reliability, better efficiency, and power outputs of 180hp or 225hp.

historyTimeline.h2: Peugeot 508 1.6 THP - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The 1.6 THP (Turbo High Pressure) arrived with the first-generation Peugeot 508 in 2010 as the performance-oriented petrol option. Based on the Prince engine family co-developed with BMW, it delivered responsive turbocharged performance across 150hp, 156hp and 165hp variants before being replaced by the PureTech family on the second-generation 508.

milestones.description: EP6DT (1.6L, 150hp) launched with the original Gen 1 508 saloon
EP6DT (1.6L, 156hp) introduced as the core THP variant for GT and GT Line trims
EP6CDT (1.6L, 163hp/165hp) added as a higher-output option
Facelift styling with minor calibration updates; THP continues
EP6DT (1.6L, 202hp) introduced as the range-topping petrol option
1.6 THP discontinued on Gen 2 508, replaced by 1.6 PureTech

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Peugeot 508 1.6 THP is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Peugeot 508 1.6 THP Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Peugeot 508 1.6 THP is a responsive turbocharged petrol engine, but timing chain tensioner failure, turbocharger oil leaks and increased oil consumption dominate replacement enquiries - the early THP generation is widely regarded as the most problematic petrol engine fitted to the 508. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Use the problem groups below to compare repair costs versus replacement value for your specific 1.6 THP.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Failure - Why EP6DT 1.6 THP Engines Rattle on Cold Start
problems.rootCause: The hydraulic timing chain tensioner loses pressure, allowing chain slack. This causes a characteristic rattling noise on cold starts lasting 2-3 seconds. On this interference-design engine, a snapped chain means valve-to-piston contact and catastrophic engine damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace tensioner, guides, chain; reset ECU adaptation
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught before noise worsens; prevents catastrophic failure

repairOptions.tier: Intermediate - Cylinder Head Inspection + Chain Kit
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove head to inspect valves; replace damaged components + full chain system
repairOptions.longevity: Appropriate if early valve contact suspected; adds cost uncertainty

repairOptions.tier: Full Replacement - Rebuilt EP6DT with Upgraded Tensioner
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt EP6DT unit with upgraded tensioner, dyno tested, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Best value when valves damaged or engine has 75k+ miles; eliminates repeat risk

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Peugeot 508 1.6 THP of 2011-2016 vintage is worth approximately £4,000-£12,000 depending on mileage and condition [INDUSTRY ESTIMATE]. For vehicles worth £4,000-£8,000, a chain kit replacement or used engine typically offers better value than a full rebuilt unit. For vehicles worth over £8,000, a rebuilt engine with upgraded timing components justifies the premium via warranty and reliability. Owners have reported repair bills exceeding £3,500 for timing chain failure on these engines.
problems.recommendation: On a Peugeot 508 1.6 THP, preventative chain replacement at the first sign of cold-start rattle is critical and cost-effective. These engines are interference designs - a snapped chain is catastrophic. If rattling is present or a compression test shows valve damage, a rebuilt engine with upgraded tensioner is the safer long-term investment. Regular oil changes every 8,000-10,000 km (5,000-6,000 miles) using fully synthetic 0W-30 oil can help extend timing chain life.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt EP6DT Peugeot 508 1.6 THP engine prices

problems.h4: Turbocharger Oil Feed Pipe Leak - Why 1.6 THP Engines Burn Oil and Smoke
problems.rootCause: The turbocharger oil feed pipe can degrade, allowing oil to leak into the exhaust or intake. This causes blue smoke from the exhaust, increased oil consumption, and potential catalytic converter damage.

repairOptions.tier: Minor - Turbo Oil Feed Pipe Replacement
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace degraded oil lines; clean intake; reset adaptation
repairOptions.longevity: Temporary fix if turbo bearings still sound; may delay but not prevent eventual turbo replacement

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove old turbo; fit new/remanufactured unit; calibrate wastegate; road test
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if engine otherwise healthy; adds cost of labour and ancillary parts

repairOptions.tier: Full Replacement - Rebuilt EP6DT with Upgraded Turbo
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt engine with upgraded turbo, updated oil lines, dyno tested, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Best value when engine has 90k+ miles or shows additional wear; eliminates repeat turbo failure risk

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a Peugeot 508 1.6 THP worth £4,000-£12,000, turbo replacement is cost-effective if the engine is otherwise sound. For higher-mileage examples or vehicles with additional oil consumption signs, a rebuilt EP6DT unit with upgraded turbo components offers better long-term value.
problems.recommendation: If your 1.6 THP shows blue smoke or increased oil consumption, have the turbo oil feed pipe inspected immediately. Replacing the pipe is a relatively low-cost intervention. If the turbo itself is damaged or the vehicle has exceeded 90,000 miles, a rebuilt engine with upgraded turbo components eliminates repeat risk.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt EP6DT Peugeot 508 1.6 THP engine prices

problems.h4: Increased Oil Consumption - Why 1.6 THP Engines Use More Oil Than Expected
problems.rootCause: A combination of turbocharger seal wear, piston ring carbonisation, and valve stem seal degradation can lead to increased oil consumption on the THP family. The early THP generation is known for this issue.

repairOptions.tier: Minor - Oil Consumption Test + PCV Valve Replacement
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Perform oil consumption test; replace PCV valve; inspect for leaks
repairOptions.longevity: First step in diagnosis; may identify simple fix

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove cylinder head; replace valve stem seals; reassemble
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if seals are the primary cause; requires specialist tooling

repairOptions.tier: Full Replacement - Rebuilt EP6DT with Upgraded Seals
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt engine with upgraded piston rings, valve seals and turbo components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Best value when engine has 100k+ miles or shows multiple wear indicators

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a Peugeot 508 1.6 THP, oil consumption of 1 litre per 1,000 miles or more warrants investigation. If the vehicle is worth under £4,000 and oil consumption is severe, a used engine may be the most cost-effective solution.
problems.recommendation: Monitor oil levels regularly on any 1.6 THP - these engines are known to consume oil. If consumption exceeds 1 litre per 1,000 miles, have a specialist perform a diagnostic. For high-mileage vehicles with multiple issues (timing chain + oil consumption + turbo wear), a rebuilt engine offers the most predictable long-term solution.
